# PlayTheory

> PlayTheory (playtheoryhq.com, also called PlayTheory HQ) is a free website of two-player strategy games that run in the browser. The games available now are DuSoKu, a two-player sudoku; Amazons, a board game of moving queens and flaming arrows; Exed-Out, tic-tac-toe on several boards where both players draw X; and Hollow, a numbers game on a triangle of hexagons. Random mode deals one game after another at random and keeps score across the run. No sign-up and nothing to install.

## DuSoKu

- Both players fill in the same sudoku puzzle. Each correct number scores points; numbers with more copies left to place are worth more.
- Each puzzle has four ×3 and eight ×2 bonus squares. A wrong number costs 1 point.
- The higher score wins when the board is full or the clock runs out. Games last at most 12 minutes.
- Play side by side on one screen, or online: send a friend a challenge link or a 5-letter room code.
- Works on phones, tablets and computers in any modern browser.

## Amazons

- Each player has two amazons that move like chess queens, then shoot an arrow that burns a square. Whoever makes the last move wins.
- A small 5×5 or 6×6 board. Each player has 4 minutes on a chess clock and at most 20 seconds a move; take longer and the turn passes, run out of time and you lose.
- Play on one screen or online with a link or room code. Online games between signed-in players are rated.

## Exed-Out

- Three to five tic-tac-toe boards. Both players draw X, anywhere on an open board.
- Three in a row closes a board. Whoever makes three in a row on the last open board loses.
- Each player has 1 minute per board on a chess clock.

## Hollow

- A triangle of 21 hexagons. Players take turns placing their numbers 1 to 10, in order.
- One hexagon stays empty. The player whose numbers around it add up to less wins; equal totals draw.
- Each player has 4 minutes on a chess clock.
